punchline: Usain Bolt took naps in the hours before breaking the world record.
thirty_sec: Matthew Walker's lab found that motor skills you practice by day get sharpened at night, mostly in the last two hours of an eight-hour sleep, which is exactly what an early alarm cuts. He shows sports teams Andre Iguodala's tracker data: after nights of more than eight hours, 29 percent more points per minute and far fewer turnovers and fouls.
